items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: Well, Chris was a blues player, yeah. He used to play blues, man.

ctx.x: Yeah. Or xylophone and then band. Yeah, let's pick that up. Let's pick it up. Well the xylophone is similar to the piano, you see. If you know the chords on the piano, you can come in there playing the xylophone, because it's just like a piano keyboard, you know. But the trombone, I just took it and I knew the bass cleft and everything, you see. All I get, I learned the positions on the horn and that was all, you see. See, it's just like the violin, it's got seven positions, you know.
Do you remember any of the trumpet players like Buddy Petit and Chris Kelly?

Yeah, Chris Kelly, Buddy Petit, Rene, now he would have made a nice trumpet player that boy, if he hadn't got the proper schooling, you know. He was better than Buddy Petit. Rene, he was very good. But he was too much of a musician, but he could play the horn nice, you know, like Louis, you know. Had a nice time? Yeah, a nice, very nice time. What kind of jobs did he play? Nothing but dances, you know, like we played. Maybe one of the little nightclubs, you know. During the war he played down at the, what's the…
